sections.heading: Locations
sections.text:
Cities and havens are together referred to as locations.
Any card that specitically talks about a city cannot be
used on a haven, and vice-versa.
Locations close to water have an anchor symbol on
them; those are port locations.

sections.heading: Havens
sections.text:

symbol are called havens. At the
beginning of your campaign,

board (be cool and come up with

sections.heading: Supply Lines
sections.text:
Although there are no supply lines at the beginning
of the game, cities will be connected to each other
across land by supply lines. Cities directly connected by
a supply line are adjacent.

sections.heading: Sea Lanes & Sea Routes
sections.text:
Locations are connected to each other in the ocean by
sea lanes. Locations directly connected by a sea lane
are adjacent. A series of connected sea lanes is called
a sea route.

sections.heading: The Grid
sections.text:
The board is largely empty as the world is mostly
unknown to you.
"The grid" refers to any location that
is connected to the starting havens (l.e., a path can
be traced along supply lines and/or sea lanes to the
starting havens).

sections.heading: Expanding the Grid
sections.text:
As you explore the world, you will expand the grid.
Whenever you open a sticker that expands the world
map, add that sticker to the board, aligning it using the
latitude and longitude lines.
OBJECTIVES

sections.heading: Objectives Section
sections.text:
In one corner of the board is a section
where objectives are placed. January
6
will start with two objectives.
Other objectives will be added and
removed in future months. If you ever have more
objectives than you can fit into this section, place some
next to the board.

sections.heading: Game End Area
sections.text:
During the game, you may be instructed to put cards
into the Game End area. At the game's end, remove all
cards from this area and follow the instructions on each
of them.

sections.heading: Incident Track
sections.text:
The Incident track lets you track how many
times a Plague cube has been placed
into a location. Even if a card or ability
removes these cubes from the world, the
Incident marker never moves backward.
When the Incident marker reaches the end
of the track, the players immediately lose
the game.

sections.heading: Supply Cube Stockpile
sections.text:
This is where Supply cubes go so that players can keep
track of how many are left and easily reach them.
During the game, unless a card or effect says otherwise,
Supply cubes are taken from and returned to the
stockpile. When an effect instructs a player to spend
1 or more Supply cubes, they take them from their
Character card and return them to the stockpile.
At the end of the game, return all Supply cubes in the
stockpile to the reserve-they do not carry over from
game to game.
STOCKPILE
